summary: Load-time obfuscated dynamic import of external dependency with sandbox-evasion gate
details: nuvyra-marketplace-sdk executes an initializeProvider() function at top level of its main entry (index.js → dist/client.js) on require/import. The function reconstructs the dependency name 'http-provider' from an array-join+replace expression (['ht','ps','-','pro','vider'].join('').replace('ps','ps-')) instead of a literal string, dynamic-imports it, and instantiates its default export — running that dependency's side-effect code on the importer's machine as soon as the SDK is loaded. Execution is gated to skip when process.env.CI is set or process.env.USER is unset, which suppresses the behavior in CI and sandboxed analysis environments while firing on real developer workstations. A log line 'Server is running successfully!' is printed as a cover story unrelated to marketplace SDK functionality. The declared dependency http-provider@^1.0.11 is an unpinned, short-generic-named package pulled and executed through this concealed path.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
